column1: Andy Burnham, Prime Minister (Labour (Co-op), Makerfield)
column9: THE ADDRESSEE. 29 Jul 2026 care-home speech: assisted dying cannot be debated until "the fixing of the funding of palliative care and social care" — "that's the position that I will stick to". 28 Aug letter to PLP: abstaining at Second Reading, will "lead a Government that implements the will of Parliament in this area – whether that is to change the law or not". Did not vote 11 Sep 2026 (2R rejected 270–286). No Commons record on the area in the ledger (from Feb 2026). Deeds so far: Casey report brought forward to summer 2027; new ministerial group (Chancellor, Housing Sec); Big Conversation on Care to Apr 2027; Fair Pay Agreement to be broadened. No money named. Placed + for words on our side, deeds pending. Leader's speech Tue 29 Sep, Liverpool. Routes in: PPS David Baines (No x3), PPSs Nic Dakin and Jo Platt (Aye x3).

column1: John Healey, Chancellor of the Exchequer (Labour, Rawmarsh and Conisbrough)
column9: WRITES THE BUDGET, 28 Oct 2026 (his first). Voted Aye 2R 29 Nov 2024 and Aye 3R 20 Jun 2025; not recorded 11 Sep 2026. No hospice or palliative record in the ledger. Test 1 (recurring hospice revenue, NHS contracts) is decided in his red box. Conference speech Mon 28 Sep. Placed - : guards the purse, voted for the Bill, no care record.

column1: Emma Reynolds, Chief Secretary to the Treasury (Labour, Wycombe)
column9: SIGNS THE SPENDING LINE. Voted Aye 2R 2024, Aye 3R 2025, Aye 2R 11 Sep 2026; voted against most safeguard amendments in 2025. A recurring £112.5m for hospices is a Chief Secretary decision. No care record. Placed - .

column1: Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care (Labour, Pontefract, Castleford and Knottingley)
column9: OWNS TEST 2. Voted Aye 2R 2024, Aye 3R 2025, Aye 2R 11 Sep 2026. Health Secretary since 20 Jul 2026; owns the Modern Service Framework for palliative and end-of-life care (promised autumn 2026, written statement 4 Jun 2026) and hospice contracting by ICBs. Her department answered Wendy Morton's hospice finance PQs 26030/26032/26033 on 7 Sep 2026 and Vikki Slade's PQ 27682 on referral-on-diagnosis on 11 Sep. No personal palliative record. Placed - .

column1: Alison McGovern, Minister of State for Care (Labour, Birkenhead)
column9: OWNS SOCIAL CARE and the day-to-day of the PM's ministerial group. Appointed 22 Jul 2026 (succeeded Stephen Kinnock). Voted Aye 2R 2024, Aye 3R 2025, Aye 2R 11 Sep 2026; voted against safeguard amendments Jun 2025. No palliative or hospice record in the ledger. Birkenhead constituency office is across the Mersey from conference: a same-morning delivery option on 29 Sep. Placed - .

column1: Karin Smyth, Minister of State for Health (Labour, Bristol South)
column9: CONFLICTING SIGNALS. Voted Aye at all three readings (2024, 2025, 11 Sep 2026), but is the minister who answers for hospices: replied for the Government in Rachael Maskell's palliative care debate 5 Mar 2026 ("immediately on opposite sides of the assisted dying debate, and we remain so. Although the Government are...") and spoke again 16 Jul 2026; ledger scores her care contributions with us. Most likely respondent to the petition. Placed 0; target Y because she is the door the answer comes through.

column1: Dame Diana Johnson, Minister of State (Labour, Kingston upon Hull North and Cottingham)
column9: Voted Aye 2R 2024, Aye 3R 2025, Aye 2R 11 Sep 2026. DHSC Minister of State from Jul 2026; no care record in the ledger. Placed - .

column1: James Frith, Parliamentary Under-Secretary for Health Innovation and Safety (Labour, Bury North)
column9: Voted No at all three readings (2024, 2025, 11 Sep 2026). Junior DHSC minister; a sympathetic voice inside the department with no purse. Placed + .

column1: Baroness Merron, Parliamentary Under-Secretary (Lords) (Labour)
column9: Speaks for DHSC in the Lords, where any Framework debate will also run. Peers are outside the Commons roster; no ledger placement. Placed 0 (no record).

column1: Angela Rayner, Housing Secretary (Labour, Ashton-under-Lyne)
column9: SENIOR ALLY ON THE MINISTERIAL GROUP. Voted No 2R 2024, No 3R 2025, No 2R 11 Sep 2026. The PM's 29 Jul announcement named the Housing Secretary on the new social care ministerial group alongside the Chancellor. The most senior Cabinet member on our side of the vote with a seat at the care table. Placed ++; ask her to press inside the group for Test 1.

column1: Wes Streeting, Defence Secretary (Labour, Ilford North)
column9: Voted No 2R 2024, No 3R 2025, No 2R 11 Sep 2026 (backed safeguard amendments in 2025). As Health Secretary delivered the £100m hospice capital and £26m children's hospice revenue (Dec 2024) and said publicly he would vote no because palliative care was not good enough. Now outside the money chain but the most quotable Cabinet voice for our framing. Placed ++.

column1: Shabana Mahmood, Home Secretary (Labour, Birmingham Ladywood)
column9: Voted No at all three readings; backed safeguard amendments Jun 2025. Cabinet ally, not on the care group, no palliative record. Placed + .

column1: Bridget Phillipson, Minister for Women and Equalities (Labour, Houghton and Sunderland South)
column9: Voted No 2R 2024, No 3R 2025, No 2R 11 Sep 2026; spoke on assisted dying at Topical Questions 9 Sep 2026 (neutral). Cabinet ally; was a named target of our Nov 2024 petition (14334, 4,288 sigs). Placed + .

column1: Louise Haigh, First Secretary of State (Labour, Sheffield Heeley)
column9: Voted Aye 2R 2024 and Aye 3R 2025; not recorded 11 Sep 2026. Runs the Cabinet Office; no care record. Placed - .

column1: Sir Alan Campbell, Leader of the House of Commons (Labour, Tynemouth)
column9: Voted Aye at all three readings. Controls Commons time; relevant to the guardrail (any returning Bill needs time he allocates), not to the care ask. Placed - .

column1: Anneliese Midgley, Government Chief Whip (Labour, Knowsley)
column9: Voted No at all three readings. Sits in Cabinet as Chief Whip; an ally in the whips' office when the Budget resolutions are whipped. Placed + .

column1: Stephen Kinnock, Welsh Secretary (Labour, Aberafan Maesteg)
column9: CONFLICTING SIGNALS. Voted Aye at all three readings and against safeguard amendments in 2025, but as Minister for Care told the Health and Social Care Committee of a further £25m hospice capital on top of the £100m. Delivered hospice money while backing the Bill. Placed 0.

column1: Sir Stephen Timms, Minister of State for Social Security and Disability (Labour, East Ham)
column9: Voted No at all three readings. Portfolio spans DWP and HCLG; disability groups (Not Dead Yet UK, BuDS) welcomed the PM's care-first line. Placed + .

column1: Florence Eshalomi, Minister of State, Housing, Communities and Local Government (Labour (Co-op), Vauxhall and Camberwell Green)
column9: Voted No 3R 2025 and No 2R 11 Sep 2026. Local government funds adult social care; an ally in the department that will carry Test 3. Placed + .

column1: Jim McMahon, Parliamentary Under-Secretary, Housing, Communities and Local Government (Labour (Co-op), Oldham West, Chadderton and Royton)
column9: Voted No at all three readings. Local government portfolio; ally. Placed + .

column1: James Murray, Financial Secretary to the Treasury (Labour, Ealing North)
column9: Voted Aye at all three readings. Health Secretary 14 May–20 Jul 2026, so briefly held the hospice file; now Treasury. No care record. Placed - .

column1: Lucy Rigby, Economic Secretary to the Treasury (Labour, Northampton North)
column9: Voted Aye at all three readings; against safeguard amendments Jun 2025. Treasury; no care record. Placed - .

column1: Dan Tomlinson, Exchequer Secretary to the Treasury (Labour, Chipping Barnet)
column9: Voted No 2R 2024, No 3R 2025, No 2R 11 Sep 2026; backed safeguard amendments Jun 2025. The one Treasury minister on our side of the vote. Placed + ; a quiet route into the Budget process.

column1: Torsten Bell, Minister of State for Pensions (Treasury and DWP) (Labour, Swansea West)
column9: Voted Aye at all three readings; against safeguard amendments Jun 2025. Treasury; no care record. Placed - .

column1: Pat McFadden, Work and Pensions Secretary (Labour, Wolverhampton South East)
column9: Voted Aye 2R 2024, Aye 3R 2025, Aye 2R 11 Sep 2026. Cabinet; carers' benefits sit with him but no care record. Placed - .

column1: Alex Norris, Lord Chancellor and Justice Secretary (Labour (Co-op), Nottingham North and Kimberley)
column9: Voted Aye at all three readings. MoJ would own the machinery of any future Bill; not a care decision-maker. Placed - ; listed for the guardrail.
